Search Query: I am trying to learn more about merge conflicts in git and how to resolve them. It would be really helpful if you could help me understand different commands like rebase and stash with examples, and make these concepts clearer to me. Also, tell me what a detached HEAD state is and how to bypass it.

- n1 -- After editing, run git add <file> then git commit -- vital
- n2 -- Git rebase moves your branch commits onto a new base commit -- vital
- n3 -- Command: git rebase master to update feature branch with latest master -- vital
- n4 -- Interactive rebase: git rebase -i master lets you reorder, squash, drop commits -- okay
- n5 -- Stash saves uncommitted working directory changes: git stash -- vital
- n6 -- Restore stashed changes: git stash pop -- vital
- n7 -- Detached HEAD means not on any branch; HEAD points to a commit -- vital
- n8 -- Exiting detached HEAD: git checkout master (or another branch) -- vital
- n9 -- From detached HEAD, start a new branch: git checkout -b newbranch -- vital
- n10 -- Conflict markers: <<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>> to distinguish local and incoming changes -- vital
- n11 -- Visual conflict resolution: git mergetool -- okay
- n12 -- Use git diff to inspect differences in a conflicted file -- vital
- n13 -- Rebase rewrites history; after rebase push with --force-with-lease -- vital
- n14 -- During rebase conflict, resolve, git add <file>, then git rebase --continue -- vital
- n15 -- Keep both changes by removing markers and committing -- vital
- n16 -- Stash with description: git stash push -m "message" -- vital
- n17 -- List stashes: git stash list -- vital
- n18 -- Drop a stash: git stash drop stash@{0} -- okay
- n19 -- Use git stash apply if you want to keep stash entry -- vital
- n20 -- Pull before push reduces merge conflicts -- okay
- n21 -- View existing branches with git branch -- okay
